title: Grove — learning made clear
question: A fresh direction after reviewing 12 learning apps and the live Grove app. Every option replaces the crowded shell: three starting routes, one next lesson, four visible skills, reversible skips, and fewer duplicate pages. Choose the learning experience and visual character to build; code-first is saved.

options.label: Practice rhythm
options.thesis: A clear course home leads to a focused session with a visible learn → practise → check sequence.
materials: spruce navigation on a mint working ground
humanist sans and solid task surfaces
options.viewport: Desktop: compact navigation, the next lesson and one Start button, then optional review; no metrics rail. Phone: home and account in the header, four labelled skills below, and the same next lesson.
options.risk: The step strip must stay simple; turning it into another progress dashboard would undo the benefit.

raised.raise: Feedback shows what was checked, rather than a decorative score.
Session controls keep their positions as task state changes.
One useful lesson title leads; repeated summaries disappear.
Return to the current course position is always visible.
Reserved feedback space keeps the next action from jumping.

options.label: Everyday phrases
options.thesis: A welcoming home makes the next useful lesson obvious, with direct practice in any of the four skills.
materials: plum navigation and a pale lilac ground
clear sans with phrase-sized lesson headings
options.viewport: Desktop: a slim top header, next lesson with Start and a quiet course-change link, then four skill choices. Phone: the next lesson sits above a compact 2×2 skill launcher; the persistent four-skill bar stays labelled.
options.risk: This is a familiar guided-learning arrangement; its distinction comes from crisp teaching and interaction rather than unusual composition.

options.label: Immersion stage
options.thesis: One activity owns the working area, with its text, audio and response kept together.
materials: an ink navigation frame around a readable task
compact sans, captions and standard controls
options.viewport: Desktop: four skill tabs, a home/course return, then one large reading or listening task with source and response controls. Phone: one task fills the working area; labelled skills and Next remain explicit buttons.
options.case: Familiar media focus makes short practice inviting; course orientation and long writing are less immediate than in the guided alternatives.
options.risk: It needs a strong course return and a sensible starter sequence so learning never becomes an endless feed.

options.label: Monochrome product proof
options.thesis: A neutral lesson and its checked answer are paired in a strict grid.
options.viewport: Standard skills surround a lesson with evidence beside it; the pair stacks on phones.
options.case: Proof panels compete with the task and the marketing character has little connection to beginner study.
options.kept: Show the checked evidence in feedback.
options.risk: A lesson can become a product display instead of useful practice.

options.label: Goldenrod timetable
options.thesis: Stable state cells and a single-size rhythm keep task changes legible.
options.viewport: Standard navigation leads a readable practice pane with stable state positions.
options.case: Travel notation is remote from reflective study; raked surfaces complicate long Russian text.
options.kept: Keep control positions stable between session states.
options.risk: Timetable character can obscure the reading hierarchy.

options.label: Saville catalogue
options.thesis: One decisive lesson title leads a sparse ink surface.
options.viewport: A conventional shell gives one lesson the visual lead, with every destination labelled.
options.case: Coded catalogue graphics weaken novice identification and destination recognition.
options.kept: Remove competing titles and repeated summaries.
options.risk: Coded identity and hover decoding cannot replace clear controls.

options.label: Midnight transit graphics
options.thesis: A visible course position makes returning to the next lesson easy.
options.viewport: Standard skills flank a lesson, with a compact course return rather than a network.
options.case: A network adds information to a home whose main job is choosing one activity.
options.kept: Always expose a return to the current course position.
options.risk: Route graphics can recreate the clutter being removed.

options.label: Split-flap concourse
options.thesis: Reserved state space makes feedback changes predictable.
options.viewport: A conventional session keeps action and feedback in stable positions.
options.case: Departure-board density and cascading letters slow reading without helping the task.
options.kept: Feedback never moves the next-action control.
options.risk: Novelty animation can overpower a simple correction.

canonCard.label: Familiar guided learning
canonCard.thesis: A straightforward course home and labelled practice destinations, executed to the quality of leading learning apps.
materials: comfortable sans and a restrained course list
canonCard.viewport: One Continue action, four skills, and a course/review menu; no competing dashboard. Phone navigation stays labelled.
canonCard.risk: Efficient and recognisable, with deliberately little individual visual character.
